map.center: Usamos HAVE BEEN + -ING para acciones que empezaron en el pasado y siguen o acaban de parar.

explain.es: El present perfect continuous (have / has been + -ing) une el pasado con el presente. Lo usamos para una actividad que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora, o que acaba de terminar y cuyos efectos todavía se notan. En español solemos decirlo con «llevar + tiempo + gerundio» o con el presente: Llevo dos horas estudiando · Estudio inglés desde 2020. ¡En inglés el presente no vale aquí!
explain.en: The present perfect continuous connects the past and the present. We use it for an activity that started in the past and is still going on, or that has just stopped and we can still see the results.

explain.title: Truco del «LLEVAR»
explain.es: Si en español dirías «llevo / llevas / lleva + tiempo + -ando / -iendo», en inglés casi siempre es have / has been + -ing: Llevo un año ahorrando → I've been saving for a year. Si preguntas «¿Cuánto tiempo llevas…?» → How long have you been…? Pero si la frase cuenta cosas (tres libros, cinco emails) → vuelve al simple.
explain.en: If in Spanish you'd say «llevo + time + -ando», use have been + -ing. If you count things, use the simple.

explain.title: 1 · Afirmativa
explain.es: Con I, you, we, they → have been; con he, she, it → has been. Been no cambia nunca y el verbo principal siempre lleva -ing. Al hablar casi siempre contraemos: I've been, she's been, they've been.
explain.en: I / you / we / they → have been; he / she / it → has been. Been never changes and the main verb always takes -ing. In speech we use short forms.
formula: I / you / we / they + *have been* + working

examples.en: I've been working on this project since January.
examples.es: Llevo trabajando en este proyecto desde enero.

examples.en: She's been learning Korean for six months.
We've been saving money for a trip to Japan.
examples.es: Hemos estado ahorrando para un viaje a Japón.

explain.title: 2 · Negativa
explain.es: not va detrás de have / has: haven't / hasn't been + -ing. ¡Nunca don't ni no! Muy útil con lately / recently (últimamente).
explain.en: Put not after have / has. Never use don't or no.
formula: I / you / we / they + *haven't been* + sleeping

examples.en: He hasn't been feeling well since Friday.
examples.es: No se encuentra bien desde el viernes.

examples.en: They haven't been answering their phones all morning.
examples.es: Llevan toda la mañana sin coger el teléfono.

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas y respuestas cortas
explain.es: Have / Has va delante del sujeto. Pregunta estrella: How long have you been + -ing…? = ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas…? Respuesta corta: Yes, I have. / No, she hasn't. (sin been).
explain.en: Have / Has goes before the subject. Key question: How long have you been + -ing…?

examples.en: Has it been raining? The streets are wet.
examples.es: ¿Ha estado lloviendo? Las calles están mojadas.

examples.en: Have you been crying? — No, I've been cutting onions!
examples.es: ¿Has estado llorando? — ¡No, he estado cortando cebolla!

explain.title: 4 · Uso 1: duración (¿cuánto tiempo?)
explain.es: Para una actividad que empezó en el pasado y todavía continúa. Destacamos cuánto tiempo lleva: for + periodo (for two hours), since + punto de inicio (since 9 o'clock), all day / all morning. En español: llevo… -ando, hace… que o presente + desde hace.
explain.en: For an activity that started in the past and is still going on. We focus on how long: for + period, since + starting point, all day.

examples.en: It's been raining since this morning.
I've been looking for a new flat for three months.
examples.es: Hace tres meses que busco piso.

examples.en: They've been talking on the phone all evening.
examples.es: Llevan toda la tarde hablando por teléfono.

explain.title: 5 · Uso 2: resultado visible
explain.es: Para una actividad que acaba de terminar (o se ha interrumpido) y cuyos efectos se ven ahora: estás cansado, sucio, mojado, rojo… No importa si la acción está completa: importa la actividad que explica la situación presente.
explain.en: For an activity that has just stopped and whose results we can see now. The activity explains the present situation.

examples.en: Your hands are filthy. What have you been doing?
examples.es: Tienes las manos sucísimas. ¿Qué has estado haciendo?

examples.en: Sorry I'm late. Have you been waiting long?
examples.es: Perdona el retraso. ¿Llevas mucho rato esperando?

explain.title: ¿Simple o continuo?
explain.es: Los dos conectan pasado y presente, pero miran cosas distintas. El simple mira el resultado: qué y cuánto has hecho (how many / how much). El continuo mira la actividad y su duración: cuánto tiempo llevas (how long).
explain.en: The simple focuses on the result (what, how many). The continuous focuses on the activity and its duration (how long).

cols.head: ⏳ Continuo · actividad / cuánto tiempo
items: She's been painting: look at her hands!

items.es: ¿La acción empezó en el pasado y sigue (o acaba de parar y se nota)? → present perfect.
items.en: Started in the past and still going on (or just stopped)? → present perfect.

items.es: ¿Te importa la actividad / duración (how long)? → continuo. ¿El resultado / cantidad (how many)? → simple.
items.en: Activity / how long → continuous. Result / how many → simple.

items.es: ¿Es un verbo de estado (know, like, want, own…)? → siempre simple.
items.en: State verb? → always simple.

items.es: Sujeto + have / has (he, she, it → has) + been + verbo-ing.
items.en: Subject + have / has + been + -ing.

items.es: Añade el tiempo: for + periodo · since + inicio · all day · lately.
items.en: Add the time: for, since, all day, lately.

lines.en: Ten! Have you found anything nice?
Not yet, but I've been checking the websites every day.

items.why: Con since / for y una acción que sigue, no se usa el presente (calco de «estudio desde…»).
items.why_en: Use the present perfect (continuous) with since / for, not the present.

items.bad: I'm waiting here for an hour.
items.good: I've been waiting here for an hour.

items.bad: I've been knowing him for years.
items.why: Know es un verbo de estado: no admite -ing.
items.why_en: Know is a state verb: no -ing.

items.bad: She's been writing five emails today.
items.why: Si cuentas cuántos (cantidad) → present perfect simple.

items.bad: How long are you living in London?
items.good: How long have you been living in London?
items.why: «¿Cuánto llevas…?» → How long + present perfect, no presente.
items.why_en: How long…? → present perfect, not present.

items.bad: We've been waiting since two hours.
items.why: for + periodo (two hours); since + momento (2 o'clock).
items.why_en: for + period; since + point in time.

items.bad: He has been work all morning.
items.why: Después de been, el verbo va siempre en -ing.

explain.title: Simple vs continuo: guía rápida
head: Fíjate en… · Look at
Present perfect simple
Present perfect continuous
rows: El resultado: I've fixed the bike. (ya funciona)
La actividad: I've been fixing the bike. (tengo las manos negras)
How many / how much: I've drunk three coffees.
How long: I've been drinking coffee all morning.
Sí, completo: I've written the report.
No necesariamente: I've been writing the report.
Permanente: He's lived in Madrid all his life.
Temporal: He's been living with friends since May.
know, like, believe, own… → I've known her for years.
I've lived here for ten years. ✓
I've been living here for ten years. ✓ (¡las dos valen!)
explain.note: Con live, work, study, teach + for / since las dos formas suelen ser correctas; el continuo suena más «en curso» o temporal.
explain.note_en: With live, work, study, teach + for / since both forms are usually fine.

exercises.text_title: Carmen's blog: a new life in Edinburgh
text: Hi everyone! It's been a while since my last post. I moved to Edinburgh last spring, so I've been living here for about eight months now. I've been working as a nurse at a big hospital since September. I love it, but I've been doing a lot of night shifts lately!

My English has improved a lot. I've been taking classes twice a week, and I've already passed two mock exams for my B2 First. The only problem is the weather: it's been raining non-stop for three days! I've bought two umbrellas this week and I've lost both of them.

My flatmate, Fiona, has been teaching me some Scottish words. She's from Glasgow and we've known each other since my first week here. My parents are coming to visit next month, and I've been planning their trip for weeks.

items.q: Carmen has been living in Edinburgh for more than a year.

items.q: Why does Carmen write 'we've known' and not 'we've been knowing'?
items.a: Because know is a state verb (no -ing).

checklist.es: Formo el present perfect continuous: have / has been + -ing.
checklist.en: I can form the present perfect continuous.

checklist.es: Lo uso para acciones que empezaron en el pasado y siguen (for, since, all day).
checklist.en: I use it for actions that started in the past and continue.

checklist.es: Explico resultados visibles: You're wet — I've been running.
Pregunto con How long have you been…?
checklist.en: I can ask How long have you been…?
I know when to use the simple and the continuous.

checklist.es: No uso -ing con verbos de estado: I've known her for years.
checklist.en: I don't use -ing with state verbs.

checklist.es: Nunca digo <s>I am living here since 2020</s>.
checklist.en: I never use the present with since / for.
